policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads simply 'Christ suffered in the flesh' with no beneficiary phrase; the added ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν would require 'for us', which the ASV text and margin lack.
'he that hath suffered in the flesh' renders a bare dative σαρκὶ and ἐν σαρκὶ identically; no ASV wording or note distinguishes the preposition.
ASV text 'hath ceased from sin' renders the genitive ἁμαρτίας; the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read unto sins' places the dative ἁμαρτίαις in the margin, not the text.
ASV 'the time past may suffice' has no indirect object; the added ἡμῖν would give 'may suffice us', which the ASV does not render.
ASV reads 'the time past' with no qualifier; τοῦ βίου would require 'of our life' or 'of life', absent from text and margin.
'the desire of the Gentiles' renders βούλημα and θέλημα alike; the ASV supplies no note distinguishing the synonyms.
'to have wrought' is a perfect English infinitive that serves the perfect κατειργάσθαι and the aorist κατεργάσασθαι equally after 'may suffice'.
ASV 'him that is ready to judge' renders the periphrasis ἑτοίμως ἔχοντι with the infinitive κρῖναι; the participle κρίνοντι would give 'him that readily judgeth'.
ASV 'unto prayer' with the gloss 'Greek prayers' shows the plural noun but not whether the Greek article τάς stood before it; English drops the article either way.
ASV begins 'above all things' with no connective, but the ASV routinely leaves a continuative δέ untranslated in a running series of exhortations, so the English does not exclude it.
ASV 'love covereth a multitude of sins' is present tense, rendering καλύπτει; the future καλύψει would give 'shall cover'.
'without murmuring' is an English mass noun that renders the singular γογγυσμοῦ and the plural γογγυσμῶν alike; no note marks the number.
ASV 'of the strength which God supplieth' renders a relative pronoun ἧς attached to ἰσχύος; the comparative ὡς would not yield 'which'.
ASV ends the verse at 'resteth upon you'; the long addition 'on their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified' appears in neither the text nor a margin.
ASV 'let him glorify God in this name' renders ὀνόματι; μέρει would give 'in this behalf/part'.
ASV 'And if the righteous' renders καὶ εἰ; an added postpositive δέ would be absorbed by the same 'And' and is not excluded by the English.
ASV commits the souls 'unto a faithful Creator' without the comparative 'as unto', which ὡς πιστῷ κτίστῃ would require.
ASV reads 'their souls' with the possessive unitalicized, rendering αὐτῶν; the omission would leave 'the souls'.
